Keep in view: mockup

GitHub #137, reframed. Every image is the real app driven by Playwright, with the proposed controls inserted using the app's existing styles, so these are its true fonts, spacing and colours rather than an imitation. The window is widened the way a user would resize it. Throwaway: delete once the design is approved, as with earlier mockups.

1 · Starting it

Open ⋯ on the entry you want to look at and choose Keep in view. Then edit whatever you like. The kept entry stays put until you close it.

2 · Recommended: the second pane (1a)

The kept entry sits read-only in the right-hand pane, where a paired reference book usually goes. It uses the same read-only card as the reference pane. The header has three controls: Highlight Differences (the same label as the checkpoint panel's toggle), Swap (edit the kept entry and keep the current one in view), and Close.

3 · Highlight Differences: two ways to draw it

This is the finding that matters most. A is the real diffEntries output, drawn the way the checkpoint panel draws it today. Even on this best case, two versions of one character, it reads as word salad: “ninethirty-four, yearsWarden old,of…”. B drops the struck-out words, which are already readable in the entry being edited on the left, and keeps the kept entry's own sentences intact.

“Compared with” exists because desktop can have several cards open at once, so there is no single “entry you're editing”. It would default to the entry you last opened.

4 · When a reference book is already paired (decision 2a)

The kept entry takes over the pane. One line under the header says the reference book returns when you close it. Nothing about the pairing changes underneath.

5 · Alternatives, for comparison

1b, the floating card, covers part of the entry you're editing: here it hides the condition field and the end of the trigger box. Dragging it out of the way is the second-window problem the plan already flags.

1c, the strip, looks better than I expected. It needs no second pane, so the editor keeps full width. Its costs: it either scrolls away with the list or, made sticky, takes permanent height. A real entry runs up to 1500 characters, so it has to be cut to about two lines, and then you can't read the whole entry, which is the point of the feature.

6 · Mobile (decision 3a)

A slim In view: Elara (adult) · Show › bar sits under the editor header and opens the same full-screen peek that reference entries already use. It costs about 36px of height. Back returns to the editor. Full inline diff (A) has a better case on mobile, because the other entry isn't on screen, but it's still word salad.
